questions.q: Which is NOT one of the four main macroeconomic objectives?
questions.why: The fourth main objective is a stable current account.

questions.q: What is the UK government's inflation target?
questions.why: The Bank of England aims for CPI inflation of 2%.

questions.q: Match each policy result to the conflict it shows.
pairs: Rising incomes pull in more imports
Falling joblessness pushes up wages and prices
questions.why: Each aim can make another harder to reach.

questions.q: The importance given to different objectives changes over time.
questions.why: High inflation in the 1970s and 1980s moved it up the list, for example.

questions.q: Which is another possible objective of macroeconomic policy?
questions.why: An equitable distribution of income is another.

questions.q: Explain how a government policy to raise economic growth could worsen the current account.

ideas.label: Higher growth raises incomes and spending
So imports rise, which widens the deficit

questions.model: Faster growth raises incomes and spending. Some of that goes on imports, so imports rise and the current account deficit widens.
questions.why: Part of any rise in spending goes abroad.

tests.answer: Higher incomes lead people to buy more imports, which widens the deficit.
